Through the diligent efforts of David Holland, the IPCC WG1 and WG2 Review Editor comments have now been obtained and are now online for the firsttime. David Holland obtained the documents through a Freedom of Information request. The Review Editor comments are very revealing. In the case of the controversial deletion of the Briffa post-1960 results, Review Editor John Mitchell (of the UK Met Office) advised: The authors should be pressed to provide a convincing explanation of why the post-1960 part of the Briffa et al. In the case of the HS dispute, Review Editor Hans von Storch (a strong supporter of the HS) advised: The authors should be asked to provide a more detailed and objective discussion of the uncertainties and the divergencies between the various reconstructions. texts.full_text: The effects of graded amounts of centrally injected [intracerebroventricular, i.c.v.] oxytocin [OXT] have been studied on the steady-state level and pargyline-induced accumulation of serotonin [5-HT] in the hypothalamus, mesencephalon, and dorsal hippocampus of rats. OXT only weakly affected the steady-state level of 5-HT. The pargyline-induced accumulation, on the other hand, was inhibited by central OXT treatment. Whereas OXT inhibited 5-HT accumulation in a dose-dependent manner in the hypothalamus, the dose-response curve was shifted to the right in the mesencephalon and dorsal hippocampus. These findings suggest that OXT may play a role in modulating 5-HT neurotransmission, possibly by affecting the reuptake or synthesis of 5-HT in specific brain regions. Further research is needed to elucidate the precise mechanisms by which OXT influences 5-HT neurotransmission and the implications of these effects in physiological and pathological conditions.

The details are at section 14.8.2.4 of the C++ Standard (2003). Why? If you specialize Outer as: template <> struct Outer<int> { struct Inner { double y; }; Inner vec[3]; }; There is no way for the compiler to deduce if Outer::Inner should reference this definition or the previous one.
